exposure: Postpartum time points (2 weeks, 6 weeks, 6 months)
outcome: Feasibility of 3-D transvaginal ultrasound image texture analysis for assessing deep levator ani muscle injuries
Monitoring tissue microstructural changes in levator ani muscle
Identification of potential imaging biomarkers (texture features) associated with structural changes
cohort: The study included 15 women at high risk for levator ani muscle injuries following vaginal delivery but without muscle avulsion, and 10 women who underwent cesarean section before the second stage of labor as controls.
finding: US image texture analysis detected systematic changes in muscle echotexture between 2 and 6 weeks postpartum, suggesting its potential as an objective method for monitoring levator ani muscle recovery.
mod_finding: Larger average percentage changes in identified texture features (12.2% ± 2.3%) were observed between 2 and 6 weeks postpartum in the vaginal delivery group, compared to smaller changes (6.0% ± 1.2% in vaginal delivery group and 6.6% ± 2.3% in C-section group) between 6 weeks and 6 months.
